findings.highlight: My entire body is numb with fear.
findings.evidenceJa: 背筋はおろか、指先までギリギリと痺れさせる威圧と恐れ。
findings.governingReading: The oppressive force and fear make even Shirou’s fingertips, not merely his spine, creak with numbness.
findings.explanation: The English drops the oppressive pressure, the spine-to-fingertips range, and the grating bodily quality.

findings.highlight: an existence that’s unlike anything I’ve ever seen.
findings.evidenceJa: 以前とはまるで違う存在になっている。
findings.governingReading: The shadow has completed its transformation into an existence utterly different from what it was before.
findings.explanation: The English replaces comparison with its former state with comparison against everything Shirou has ever seen.

findings.highlight: The thing in front of us is a virtual image.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜を象っただけの虚像だった。
findings.governingReading: The wavering thing is only a false image modeled on Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English preserves unreality but drops the governing relation that the image is specifically modeled on Sakura.

findings.highlight: You’ve gotten arrogant during the short time you’ve been away.
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっと見ない間に偉くなったものね桜
findings.governingReading: Rin sarcastically says Sakura has risen in stature or become quite grand while out of sight.
findings.explanation: The English turns a taunt about Sakura’s newfound power and status into a direct personality judgment that she has become arrogant.

findings.highlight: ‘Senpai’.
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩、と。
findings.governingReading: The narration reads an unspoken “Senpai” in the look directed at Shirou.
findings.explanation: Quotation marks make the implied appeal look like dialogue Sakura actually speaks.

findings.highlight: I can’t say anything to her, as doing so would weaken my resolve.
findings.evidenceJa: ここで桜に声をかけ、わずかでも決意を弱める事はできない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot call out to Sakura here and weaken his resolve even slightly.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes calling out to saying anything and drops the carefully minimal “even slightly.”

findings.highlight: She confronts Tohsaka with a cold voice.
findings.evidenceJa: 冷たい侮蔑のこもった声で、遠坂と対峙した。
findings.governingReading: Sakura confronts Rin in a voice containing cold contempt.
findings.explanation: The English retains coldness but removes the contempt that defines Sakura’s posture toward Rin.

findings.highlight: Completely cold, showing no concern for Sakura.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜に対して一片の関心もない、見下しきった冷徹な声。
findings.governingReading: Rin’s cold voice appears to contain not a scrap of concern and to look completely down on Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English retains lack of concern but omits the total contempt in Rin’s deliberately performed voice.

findings.highlight: I won’t let him out
findings.evidenceJa: あの子は外には出しません
findings.governingReading: Sakura says she will not let “that child” outside while she remains.
findings.explanation: The English assigns male gender where this line uses a nongendered relational expression.

findings.highlight: I might only be able to hold out for one night.
findings.evidenceJa: わたしが耐えられるのは今夜だけかもしれない
findings.governingReading: Sakura may be able to endure only tonight.
findings.explanation: The English turns the specific remaining night into an abstract one-night duration.

findings.highlight: take his life with mine
findings.evidenceJa: あの子と刺し違えるコトが出来ますから
findings.governingReading: Sakura says she can destroy the entity while perishing with it.
findings.explanation: The English genders the entity and recasts mutual destruction as taking his life with hers.

findings.highlight: Sakura says she’s going to kill him using her life.
findings.evidenceJa: 刺し違える、と桜は言った。
findings.governingReading: The narration repeats Sakura’s claim that she will perish together with the entity in killing it.
findings.explanation: The English changes reciprocal destruction into using her life as a means to kill a male entity.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka trembles a bit.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の肩がわずかに震える。
findings.governingReading: Rin’s shoulder trembles slightly.
findings.explanation: The English expands the localized shoulder movement into an unspecified whole-body tremble.

findings.highlight: when you’ll run out of patience
findings.evidenceJa: いつ我慢できなくなるか判らない
findings.governingReading: Rin accuses Sakura of not knowing when she will cease to be able to endure it.
findings.explanation: “Run out of patience” psychologizes a limit of endurance as irritation or impatience.

findings.highlight: You’ll kill the Servant within the Holy Grail along with you
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯の中にいるサーヴァントも、その力を受け継いだアンタも、一緒になって死んでくれるんだ
findings.governingReading: Rin says both the Servant inside the Grail and Sakura, who inherited its power, will die together.
findings.explanation: The English makes Sakura the killer of the Servant and drops the explicit inherited-power relation.

findings.highlight: I don’t want you to see me change.
findings.evidenceJa: 変わりきる姿を見られたくない
findings.governingReading: Sakura does not want Shirou to see the form she will have when transformation is complete.
findings.explanation: The English shifts the object from her completed transformed appearance to the process of changing.

findings.highlight: it asks for salvation by letting us go
findings.evidenceJa: “追ってこないでほしい”、と救いを求める
findings.governingReading: At mortal risk, Sakura’s shadow seeks salvation in the plea that they not pursue her.
findings.explanation: The English makes the shadow grant their release as the means of salvation, reversing who is asking whom to do what.

findings.highlight: let her kill herself along with Angra Mainyu
findings.evidenceJa: アンリマユと刺し違える、という桜
findings.governingReading: Sakura proposes killing Angra Mainyu while dying in the exchange.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the reciprocal attack to Sakura killing herself alongside it.

findings.highlight: We’ll go there. We’ll go and kill you for sure.
findings.evidenceJa: 行くわ。行って、確実にアンタを殺す
findings.governingReading: Rin personally declares that she will go and certainly kill Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English repeatedly changes Rin’s singular declaration into a collective “we.”

findings.highlight: breaks away from her sister
findings.evidenceJa: 実の妹と決別した
findings.governingReading: Rin clearly breaks with her own biological younger sister.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the blood relation and Sakura’s position as the younger sister.

findings.highlight: As Tohsaka’s magus
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の魔術師として
findings.governingReading: Rin speaks in her capacity as a magus of the Tohsaka line.
findings.explanation: The English possessive makes Rin sound like a magus belonging to a person named Tohsaka.

findings.highlight: You want to kill, but you’re telling me to run.
findings.evidenceJa: わたしを殺したいクセに逃げろだなんてね
findings.governingReading: Rin highlights Sakura’s contradiction: Sakura wants to kill Rin yet tells Rin to flee.
findings.explanation: The English omits Rin as the object of the desire to kill, weakening the contradiction and their personal conflict.

findings.highlight: we’ll go see you right away
findings.evidenceJa: すぐに会いに行ってあげる
findings.governingReading: Rin says she herself will come to meet Sakura soon.
findings.explanation: The English again pluralizes Rin’s deliberately personal promise.

findings.highlight: you can make a good face
findings.evidenceJa: いい顔するじゃない
findings.governingReading: Rin approves the hostile expression Sakura finally shows.
findings.explanation: The literal “make a good face” is unnatural English and obscures the taunt’s reference to Sakura’s expression.

findings.highlight: It smiles violently
findings.evidenceJa: くすり、と凄絶なまでの笑みをこぼして
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s projection lets out a small laugh and spills a smile fierce or terrible in its intensity.
findings.explanation: “Smiles violently” is malformed and loses the contrast between the small laugh and the overwhelming smile.

findings.highlight: The shadow covering the house recedes.
findings.evidenceJa: 屋敷を覆っていた影は消えた。
findings.governingReading: The shadow that covered the mansion has disappeared.
findings.explanation: The English changes a completed disappearance into an ongoing recession.

findings.highlight: If you want to run
findings.evidenceJa: このまま町から離れるって言うのなら
findings.governingReading: Rin says she will not stop Shirou if he says he will leave the city as things stand.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the concrete proposal to leave town with generic flight.

findings.highlight: I won’t run away
findings.evidenceJa: 戦いは止めない
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he will not stop the fight.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes refusal to flee for his commitment to continue fighting.

findings.highlight: Then I’ll follow up by doing things you can’t do.
findings.evidenceJa: なら最後まで、遠坂に出来ない事をフォローする
findings.governingReading: Because they are cooperating, Shirou will support Rin through the end by covering what she cannot do.
findings.explanation: The English drops the through-the-end scope and weakens covering Rin’s limits into vaguely doing other things.

findings.highlight: be Sakura’s superhero
findings.evidenceJa: 桜にとっての正義の味方になる
findings.governingReading: Shirou resolves to become an ally or champion of justice for Sakura specifically.
findings.explanation: “Superhero” flattens the route-defining reuse and restriction of Shirou’s justice ideal.

findings.highlight: Her inquiry is decisive.
findings.evidenceJa: その言及は、決定的だった。
findings.governingReading: Rin’s explicit mention of Sakura’s killings is decisive.
findings.explanation: The English changes the decisive act from naming the fact to asking a question.

findings.highlight: A sin I can’t talk myself out of.
findings.evidenceJa: 言い逃れのできない罪。
findings.governingReading: It is a sin from which there is no evasion or excuse.
findings.explanation: The English narrows inescapability to Shirou’s ability to talk his way out of it, suggesting rhetorical evasion.

findings.highlight: including the part of her that wants to kill herself
findings.evidenceJa: 自分を殺したがっている桜もひっくるめて
findings.governingReading: Shirou will protect Sakura in her entirety, including Sakura as she is now wanting her own death.
findings.explanation: The English partitions the suicidal wish into a discrete “part of her,” adding a model of divided selfhood absent from the line.

findings.highlight: I’m able to tell her what I think.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の気持ちを、胸を張ってカタチにできた。
findings.governingReading: Shirou can proudly give his feeling a definite form.
findings.explanation: The English reduces proud articulation and embodiment to merely telling Rin what he thinks.

findings.highlight: You beat me.
findings.evidenceJa: 正直、負けたわ
findings.governingReading: Rin frankly admits that she has lost.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the victory directly to Shirou, making her self-assessment a competitive declaration about him.

findings.highlight: I’m not going to say anything now.
findings.evidenceJa: もう口出ししないわよ
findings.governingReading: Rin says she will no longer interfere or object.
findings.explanation: The English changes continuing noninterference from this point onward into not saying anything at the present moment.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka looks angry now.
findings.evidenceJa: 微妙に頬をプリプリさせている
findings.governingReading: Rin is subtly puffing or swelling her cheeks in comic irritation.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the precise, comic facial behavior with a broad assertion that she looks angry.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka leaves with that.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂は離れへ消えていった。
findings.governingReading: Rin disappears into the detached annex after her parting shot.
findings.explanation: The English omits her destination and the sense of disappearing into it.

findings.highlight: The uneasiness in my chest goes away.
findings.evidenceJa: 胸につかえていた大きな不安が溶けてくれた
findings.governingReading: A large anxiety lodged obstructively in Shirou’s chest melts away.
findings.explanation: The English preserves relief but removes the anxiety’s size, obstructive placement, and melting image.

findings.highlight: save Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: 桜をちゃんと立ち直らせてやれる
findings.governingReading: Shirou believes Rin can properly help Sakura recover and get back on her feet.
findings.explanation: The English reduces Sakura’s personal recovery and rehabilitation to generic rescue.
